title: Item rename caps at 26 characters vs DFU's TextBox default 31
claim: DFU's rename runs through DaggerfallInputMessageBox whose TextBox default maxCharacters is 31 (TextBox.cs:26), and RenameItem itself imposes no cap (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:1348-1354). The port's inline rename field (a recorded widget departure) stops accepting characters at 26 (itemMakerWindow.js:316: 'this.itemName.length < 26').
consequence: Item names 27-31 characters long, legal in DFU, cannot be typed in the port's rename strip.

title: Recipe pick partially fills the cauldron instead of refusing when ingredients are missing
claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron: if any recipe ingredient is unmatched it shows GetLocalizedText("reqIngredients") and adds NOTHING (cs:297-301); otherwise it ClearCauldron()s first, adds every ingredient, and sets nameLabel = recipeName (cs:302-308). The port's _fillFrom (potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds whatever gatherRecipe found (potions.js:229-239) - no missing-ingredient message, no cauldron clear (fills on top of existing contents), no name label. potions.js:224-228's comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse', which the C# contradicts; potionmakerwindow.test.js:180-191 pins the port behavior while citing :283-309 - the pin restates the port.
consequence: Picking a recipe while missing one herb silently loads an incomplete cauldron; mixing burns the ingredients on a useless potion, where DFU refuses with a message. Picking with leftovers in the pot also mixes them in.

title: Mixing an empty cauldron shows the failure message instead of doing nothing
claim: DFU's MixButton_OnMouseClick plays the click and only calls MixCauldron() 'if (cauldron.Count > 0)' (cs:396-397). The port's _mix (potionMakerWindow.js:151-169) has no emptiness guard: mixCauldron([]) hashes the empty list, matches no recipe, and the window shows the POTION_FAILED box ('The ingredients you have combined are useless.').
consequence: Clicking MIX (or pressing M/Enter) with an empty pot pops a failure message box that DFU never shows.

title: Enchanted ingredients are not excluded from the potion maker's list
claim: DFU's Refresh collects ingredients with 'if (item.IsIngredient && !item.IsEnchanted)' (cs:148), and the consume walk also passes allowEnchantedItem: false (cs:338, :345). The port's ingredients() (potionMakerWindow.js:125-133) filters with isIngredient(it) alone (potions.js:184 - template flag only), so an enchanted gem (mintable at the port's own item maker, which lists Gems) appears in the ingredient grid and can be added to the cauldron and consumed.
consequence: A player can grind an enchanted ruby into a potion - and the takeOne consumption may instead burn an unenchanted one - where DFU keeps enchanted items out of the pot entirely.

title: Ingredient list never scrolls: this.scroll has no writer
claim: DFU's ingredientsListScroller is a scrolling ItemListScroller (4 rows x 3 cols, cs:226-233) with scroll handling for an arbitrary ingredient count. The port initializes this.scroll = 0 (potionMakerWindow.js:113) and reads it at :216 and :234, but nothing in click() or input() ever modifies it - grep confirms those are the only three references. Only the first 12 ingredient stacks are ever shown or clickable.
consequence: A player holding more than 12 distinct ingredient stacks (routine for an alchemist) can never see or use ingredients 13+, and recipes needing them can only be loaded via the RECIPES button.

title: Adding an ingredient from a stack hides the whole stack (no SplitStack)
claim: DFU's AddToCauldron splits one unit off a stack before moving it: 'if (item.IsAStack()) item = ingredients.SplitStack(item, 1)' (cs:256-257), leaving the remainder visible and addable. The port's _addToCauldron (potionMakerWindow.js:137-141) pushes the stack OBJECT into the cauldron, and ingredients() (:125-133) removes it from the list by identity, so a stack of N elderberries vanishes entirely from the grid while one conceptual unit is in the pot; a second unit of the same stack cannot be added.
consequence: With merged ingredient stacks (the port stacks ingredients per inventory.js:110), the remaining N-1 units are invisible and unusable while one is in the cauldron; DFU shows and offers the remainder.
